findings.status: open_in_raw_snapshot; parent reports fix in progress
findings.issue: Eyewa, Grubtech and Letswork retain numeric amounts while currency is null. Kitopi's company-only funding_round claim also retains numeric amount with null currency although the event fields and separate adviser currency claim establish USD.
findings.correction: For currency-null claims set amount=null and preserve the reported dollar amount in amount_text. For Kitopi retain the separately sourced USD 415,000,000 event only if the adviser currency claim remains attached to that event; the company-only assertion must not silently borrow a currency without its provenance.

findings.finding: Walkers identifies itself as British Virgin Islands counsel on Kitopi's transaction and explicitly reports US$415 million Series C. This independently corroborates USD and amount. The company release repeatedly timed out during this review; the four founders, January 2018 founding period and 1 July 2021 event dateline were not independently re-read.
findings.correction: Retain the original research agent's sourced founder/date assertions with their existing provenance; describe the independent review limit accurately. Do not replace the claimed 2021 event dateline with the migrated 2022 page header. Leave closed_on null unless an exact closing day is separately explicit.

findings.finding: General Atlantic's dated release explicitly names Anass Boumediene and Mehdi Oudghiri as co-founders/co-CEOs and Abdullah AlRugaib as co-founder/managing director; its company description states founded 2017 and dual headquarters in Riyadh and Dubai. These are not inferred from the Riyadh dateline.
findings.correction: No factual correction. Preserve all three founders and dual HQ as of 2024-11-27; use a single canonical company identity across UAE and Saudi packets.

findings.finding: The Salica page's headline shortens the financing to Series B, but its release body explicitly says the $15 million covers Series B and Series A extension rounds. It attributes the lead Jahez investment arm and participation by Addition and Oryx Fund specifically to the Series B.
findings.correction: Retain one combined financing observation with component amounts null, reported_on 2024-05-28 and announced_on null. Do not encode a standalone $15 million Series B or assume those participants funded the A extension.

findings.finding: The current company About page explicitly states 2019 founding in Dubai by Omar AlMheiri and Hamza Khan and explicitly describes the December 2022 $2.1M seed as led by 500 Global and Sanabil Investments. The two lead names therefore are supported by the company statement, not inferred merely from accelerator participation.
findings.correction: Use: 'The current company About page reports a December 2022 seed round led by 500 Global and Sanabil Investments; the exact investing legal vehicles remain unresolved.' Preserve source names with resolved_entity_id=null and do not substitute a combined accelerator entity. Keep 2019 as the current company's assertion; retain any separate 2018 launch chronology conflict found by the commerce agent. About's Letswork Technologies LLC and Terms' Letswork LLC remain a legal-name conflict, not a resolved alias or proven incorporation relationship.
findings.remaining_gap: Original dated financing release and exact investing vehicles have not been independently verified.

findings.finding: The reproduced announcement body describes a minority investment agreement allowing ASCA to invest up to $30 million over time; it does not establish that $30 million had been funded. ASCA's own investment profile separately supplies structured equity/growth capital, Arnold Investments Fund LP and May 2023.
findings.correction: Use: 'Minority investment announced; agreement permits ASCA to invest up to $30 million over time. Amount funded at announcement is undisclosed.' Keep amount=null and currency=null. Preserve commitment cap only as an explicitly unconverted source observation, not a normalized funding amount. Keep ASCA as the event participant and Disrupt.com as a continuing shareholder only. Keep the Arnold Investments Fund LP and instrument assertions linked to ASCA's own profile instead of attributing them solely to the reproduced announcement.

findings.finding: Wamda's 29 November 2023 headline/bullets label the financing Series B; its reproduced release describes a funding round and explicitly states US$20 million. DFDF's 2026 investor release has an 11 February 2026 dateline, a 20 February page date and describes new funding ahead of a planned Series B.
findings.correction: Use: 'Wamda labels the 2023 financing Series B; its reproduced release calls it a funding round. DFDF's February 2026 release describes its new funding as ahead of a planned Series B. Preserve both dated source assertions without resolving the stage.' Keep the 2023 USD 20,000,000 amount. Keep the 2026 amount null, announced_on 2026-02-11 and published_on 2026-02-20. Do not silently restage the 2023 or 2026 event.

findings.finding: JIMCO explicitly reports US$22 million Series A participation in December 2024 and founding in 2021. Company timeline and YC say founded 2020. YC names Sarah Toukan, Faisal Toukan and Andrew Gold as founders. Company narrative includes Talal Toukan; its linked press title names the three Toukan siblings as co-founders.
